name: Retting of flax and hemp fibres
note: Water or dew retting breaks down pectin binding fibre to woody core, controlled fermentation in standing water

name: Scutching: breaking fibres from woody core
note: Scutching board and wooden scutcher blade beat retting fibre to separate long bast fibres from brittle woody break, crude mechanisation with flails

name: Hackling: combing and grading fibres
note: Pins set in flat boards, four grades of hecklers pull fibre through progressively finer pins, separates long line from short tow

name: Cotton gin: separation of seed from fibre
note: Wire hooks on rotating cylinder brush cotton past fixed blade, seeds fall away, reduces hand ginning labour by factor of fifty

name: Carding: opening and aligning fibres
note: Hand cards with bent wire teeth tease fibres, two cards with offset teeth align them parallel and remove neps, foundation of modern spinning

name: Combing: alignment of long fibres
note: Combs of progressive fineness remove short fibres and neps, produces smoother yarn than carding, only for long-staple fibres like flax and worsted

name: Gilling: parallel alignment after combing
note: Two finely-toothed combs slide over fibres held in roller nips, removes remaining short fibres and duplicates combing process

name: Drawing: fibre blending and extension
note: Two and more rovings drawn together and doubled, evens out slubs, allows fibre blending and increases draft

name: Roving frame: fibre attenuation and twist
note: Rollers at progressively faster speeds attenuate fibres, flyer imparts twist, produces roving ready for spinning frame

name: Sliver: card output and sliver can
note: Coiled card output into sliver can, preparatory to drawing frame, loose strand of carded fibres with no twist

name: Flyer: the earliest spinning frame component
note: U-shaped guide of twisted metal, draws fibre at constant rate while imparting twist, basis of all frame spinning before the ring frame

name: Bobbin and flyer assembly: early spinning
note: Bobbin holds spun yarn, flyer guides it at controlled rate, differential speed creates twist, foundation spinning geometry before ring frame

name: Cap frame spinning
note: Wooden spindle with metal cap, flyer rotates with spindle, early frame for coarser counts, easier to wind than flyer and bobbin

name: Ring frame: the dominant spinning geometry
note: Traveller slides on fixed ring, spindle rotates below, continuous yarn formation, allows higher speeds and finer counts, gradually displaced cap frame from 1870s

name: Spinning mule: draw-twist-wind
note: Carriage moves in and out, spindles move back and forth, intermittent action allows finer yarns than ring frame, handcraft for winding, steam-powered versions still require skill

name: Throstle: continuous drawing and twist
note: Ring frame with spindle speed matched to roller draft, fully continuous, better for coarser counts than mule, easier to automate than mule

name: Doubling frame: twisting multiple yarns
note: Two or more bobbins feed into single twist spindle, creates plied yarn for strength and appearance, essential for warp threads

name: Yarn count standardisation
note: Count is length per weight unit, English Cotton Count is 840 yards per pound, essential for yarn specification and trade

name: Twist insertion control
note: Twist multiplier, turns per inch, balances strength and handle, S and Z directions, critical knowledge for spinner

name: Shed: warp separation for pick insertion
note: Opening between warp threads for shuttle passage, basic concept behind all weaving machines

name: Heddle: warp thread carrier and riser
note: Metal or string loop holding warp thread, rises and falls to create shed, hand production in early looms

name: Shaft: harness frame assembly
note: Wooden frame holding heddles, multiple shafts create different shed patterns, basic hand loom has four shafts for tabby and twill

name: Dobby head: mechanical shed control
note: Pegged barrel or chain cam controls shaft raising, each peg or link controls one pick, allows complex patterns without Jacquard cost

name: Jacquard head: automatic pattern control
note: Each warp thread on independent hook, punched cards control individual hooks, enables arbitrary patterns, complex and expensive

name: Jacquard cards: pattern storage and control
note: Punched cards laced together, each row represents one pick, hole position controls hook, complex patterns require hundreds of cards

name: Shuttle: weft carrier and timing
note: Pointed boat-shaped carrier holding bobbin, travels through shed, must be timed to stop at selvage, critical for loom speed

name: Picking: mechanical shuttle propulsion
note: Rotating cam drives picker sticks that strike shuttle, replaces hand throwing, enables power loom and higher speeds

name: Take-up: woven cloth winding
note: Graduated drum winds woven cloth at controlled rate, compensates for warp tension, prevents bunching

name: Let-off: warp feed control
note: Brake on warp beam, maintains constant tension as yarn unwound, keeps warp on take-up synchronized

name: Temple: cloth width maintenance
note: Expanding frame with sharp points, maintains woven cloth width against warp tension, prevents draw-in

name: Warp sizing: fibre stiffening
note: Starch or other binder applied to warp, increases abrasion resistance and stiffness, essential for high-speed weaving

name: Warping mill: warp thread length setting
note: Large wheel and pegs set warp length and thread count, critical for accurate cloth dimensions

name: Beam: warp holder and tension
note: Heavy wooden roller wound with warp, large diameter maintains even tension, critical support structure

name: Selvedge: woven cloth edge
note: Finished edge from shuttle reversing, tighter weave than body, essential for quality cloth, achieved by plain weave turn-around

name: Automatic loom: self-threading shuttle
note: Empty shuttle automatically ejected and threaded shuttle inserted, eliminates hand threading, increases speed and reduces downtimes

name: Automatic bobbin changer: weft supply
note: Automatic supply of full bobbins when current runs out, eliminates manual bobbin replenishment, essential for unattended running

name: Stocking frame: hosiery machine
note: Reciprocating needles hold loops, springs pull down, needles rise to throw loop, produces high-quality hosiery, skilled operator control

name: Circular knitting machine: tubular production
note: Rotating bed of needles forms tube, true circular motion, enables continuous production, coarse and fine gauges

name: Warp knitting: sheet production
note: Multiple yarn guides feed warp-wise, creates sheet fabric instead of tube, less stretch than weft knitting, high speed possible

name: Latch needle: self-contained knit mechanism
note: Self-closing latch eliminates spring requirement, lighter pressure, enables higher gauge and finer yarns, invention transformed knitting

name: Scouring: removal of grease and soil
note: Hot alkali bath removes natural oils and dirt, essential preparatory step for dyeing and bleaching, caustic or soap-based

name: Fulling: cloth densification
note: Mechanical or chemical treatment matts fibres, shrinks and densifies cloth, essential for wool cloth, water-powered fulling mills

name: Milling: extended fulling
note: Continued fulling process, creates thick dense cloth, especially for woollen fabrics and felt-like handle

name: Raising: fibre napping
note: Rotating cylinder with teasel or wire brushes teases fibre ends to surface, mechanical replacement for hand teasel

name: Cropping: nap trimming
note: Rotating cylinders with sharp blades trim raised nap to uniform height, creates smooth surface, high speed continuous operation

name: Shearing: precision cutting
note: Stationary blade against rotating grooved drum cuts pile uniformly, produces velvet and pile fabrics

name: Calendering: surface pressing
note: Heated rollers under controlled pressure compact surface, produces sheen and smoothness, essential for cotton satins

name: Mercerising: caustic treatment
note: Caustic soda under tension swell and align cotton fibres, increases lustre and dye uptake, becomes permanent feature of premium cotton

name: Singeing: flame removal of nap
note: Open flame across cloth surface burns fine fibres, produces smooth finish, replaces hand holding over candle with continuous flame

name: Desizing: size removal
note: Enzymatic or chemical removal of starch sizing applied to warp, must precede dyeing and finishing

name: Bleaching by sunlight: oxidative whitening
note: Laid on grass, UV radiation breaks colour bodies, slowest method but gentlest on fibres, traditional for linen

name: Bleaching by chlorine: rapid whitening
note: Chlorine water or bleach powder oxidises colour bodies, fastest industrial method, some fibre damage especially to cotton

name: Bleaching by hydrogen peroxide: mild oxidation
note: Milder than chlorine, leaves no toxic residue, gentler on fibres, requires careful pH control, becomes preferred method by 1920s

name: Dyeing in fibre: pre-spin colouration
note: Loose fibres or cards dipped in dye bath, blends different coloured fibres before spinning, essential for heathers and mixtures

name: Dyeing in yarn: skein colouration
note: Skeins hung in dye bath, requires even access to liquor, risk of uneven colour, essential for solid-colour fabrics

name: Dyeing in piece: woven cloth colouration
note: Folded cloth in dye bath, most efficient use of dye, requires careful handling to avoid creases, standard for finished fabric

name: Dyeing in garment: finished good colouration
note: Finished garment dipped in vat, enables custom colouration, risk of shrinkage, labour-intensive due to garment complexity

name: Block printing: carved design application
note: Hand-carved wooden blocks with raised design, dipped in dye and stamped repeatedly, high labour for design creation

name: Roller printing: engraved cylinder application
note: Engraved copper roller applies pattern continuously, replaces block printing, enables fine detail and high speed, expensive engraving

name: Screen printing: mesh stencil application
note: Silk or other mesh with photographic emulsion stencil, squeegee forces dye through, emerges in 1920s for fine art and textile printing

name: Resist dyeing: pattern preservation
note: Wax or paste mask areas of cloth before dyeing, creates patterns through negative space, includes batik and tie-dye

name: Discharge printing: dye removal
note: Bleaching agent printed onto dyed cloth removes colour, creates light patterns on dark background, requires proper discharge agents

name: Waterproofing: moisture resistance
note: Oil or wax coating repels water, essential for outdoor wear, reduces breathability, various formulations tested in early 20th century

name: Flameproofing: combustion resistance
note: Chemical treatment slows combustion, essential for children's wear and upholstery, various formulations with durability challenges

name: Mothproofing: insect resistance
note: Toxic treatment repels moths, essential for wool storage, formulations including arsenic compounds, durability limited

name: Permanent press: wrinkle resistance
note: Resin cross-linking sets cloth shape, major innovation in 1930s-1940s, requires formaldehyde chemistry and heat treatment

name: Flax cultivation and fibre
note: Long bast fibres from flax plant, strongest vegetable fibre, linen production base, Mediterranean and European cultivation

name: Hemp cultivation and fibre
note: Similar to flax, coarser and stronger, rope and canvas use, European cultivation common

name: Jute cultivation and fibre
note: Indian river plant, coarse bast fibre, cheap and fast-growing, bagging and carpet use, emerges as industrial fibre in 19th century

name: Ramie cultivation and fibre
note: Asian bast fibre, fine and strong, China and India production, difficult processing limits adoption

name: Wool: sheep fibre
note: Protein fibre from sheep, natural crimp and elasticity, warmth and moisture absorption, Mediterranean and Northern European production

name: Worsted: combed wool yarn
note: Combed long-staple wool, smooth and strong, fine suiting yarns, English West Country specialty from medieval period

name: Mohair: angora goat fibre
note: Turkish angora goat fibre, lustrous and strong, luxury use, Istanbul region monopoly until late 19th century

name: Cashmere: goat undercoat fibre
note: Mongolian and Himalayan goat undercoat, extremely fine and soft, luxury fibre, Kashmir region centres of trade

name: Silk: cultivated fibre
note: Protein fibre from silkworm cocoon, continuous filament, lustrous, expensive, Asian production trademarked

name: Sericulture: silk production
note: Silkworm rearing and cocoon processing, stifling and degumming, labour-intensive, Chinese and Indian expertise

name: Wild silk: non-cultivated production
note: Silk from wild moth cocoons, shorter filament and darker colour, Tussar and Muga silks from India and China

name: Rayon by nitration: cellulose nitrate
note: Cellulose nitrate dissolved and extruded, first artificial fibre, flammable and unstable, replaced by safer cupro rayon

name: Rayon by cupro: copper-ammonia process
note: Cellulose in copper-ammonia complex spun through air, smoother than viscose, excellent silk-like lustre, emerges in 1890s

name: Rayon by viscose: alkali-carbon disulfide process
note: Most important rayon process, versatile and scalable, controls properties by coagulation bath, dominant by 1920s

name: Rayon by acetate: cellulose acetate
note: Cellulose acetate spun directly, not regenerated cellulose, safer and easier than cupro, emerges in 1920s

name: Nylon 6,6: polyamide synthesis
note: First fully synthetic fibre from petroleum, extraordinary durability and elasticity, DuPont patented 1935, launched 1940

name: Polyester: terylene synthesis
note: Polyethylene terephthalate condensation, extremely versatile, crease resistance, ICI developed pre-1950 but mass production post-war

name: Acrylic: polyacrylonitrile fibres
note: Acrylonitrile-based polymerisation, wool-like properties, developed in 1940s, emerges as major fibre by late 1940s

name: Glass fibre: silica filament
note: Fine glass filaments drawn from melt, high strength and temperature resistance, industrial applications in 1930s

name: Asbestos cloth: fire-resistant fabric
note: Woven asbestos fibres, extreme heat resistance to 1100C plus, essential for protective wear and insulation, long-term health consequences unknown

name: Eye-pointed needle: self-threading sewing
note: Needle with eye at point, thread slides in from end during forward motion, essential for mechanical sewing machines

name: Lockstitch: two-thread interlocking
note: Needle loop interlocks with bobbin loop, requires precise timing and tension, most important sewing machine invention

name: Chain stitch: thread-only interlocking
note: Single needle thread creates loops, used in early machines and special applications, less strong than lockstitch

name: Overlock: edge-covering stitch
note: Multiple threads bind over edge, prevents fraying and seals edge, specialist machines emerge in 1890s

name: Buttonhole machine: eyelet cutting and binding
note: Cuts buttonhole and simultaneously binds edge with thread, replaces hand work, enables mass production of shirts

name: Cutting table: stacked cloth cutting
note: Large flat table with edge, cloth stacked and cut to pattern, enables multiple pieces from single cutting

name: Band knife: reciprocating cloth cutter
note: Motor-driven reciprocating blade cuts through stacked cloth, pattern template guides cutting, eliminates hand scissors

name: Pattern grading: multi-size scaling
note: Master patterns scaled to multiple sizes, essential for ready-to-wear, ratio grading becomes standard practice

name: Sizing systems: body measurement standardisation
note: Standard body measurements and fit models, crucial for mass production, significant variation by country and manufacturer

name: Paper pattern: home sewing pattern
note: Printed pattern pieces and instructions, mass-market product, Butterick patterns emerge in 1860s, enables home dressmaking

name: Zip fastener: metal hook closure
note: Interlocking metal teeth on two tapes, slider engages hooks, invented in 1890s but refined in 1920s for widespread adoption

name: Press stud: snap fastener
note: Four-piece metal fastener, ball and socket interlock, emerges in late 19th century, easier than buttons for infant wear

name: Hook and eye: wire fastener
note: Hand-formed wire hook and eye loop, traditional closure, essential for corsets and men's breeches

name: Elastic: rubber thread
note: Rubber covered thread or cord, recoverable stretch, essential for undergarments and sportswear, emerging in early 20th century

name: Corset: rigid body support garment
note: Boned structure shapes silhouette, whalebone and metal stays, essential women's garment from medieval through 20th century

name: Brassiere: supportive undergarment
note: Elastic-based support without rigid boning, emerges in 1910s-1920s as alternative to corset, major innovation in women's comfort

name: Ready-to-wear: mass-produced garments
note: Factory-made garments in standard sizes, replaces bespoke tailoring for most consumers, emerged mid-19th century in America

name: Sewing machine: domestic version
note: Human-powered treadle or hand crank, complex motion conversion, Singer and others dominated market, transformed home sewing

name: Sewing machine: industrial version
note: Steam or electric powered, higher speeds and heavier fabrics, multiple machines linked by belts, factory standard from 1870s

name: Rope laying: strand twisting
note: Three or more yarns twisted together, fundamental construction, creates rope from fibre strands

name: Ropemaking machine: mechanised twisting
note: Rotating frames twist strand into rope, water-powered mills standard, enables continuous production

name: Cordage for paperboard production
note: Paper pulp twisted into cord, intermediate product for paperboard and containers

name: Vegetable tanning: oak bark curing
note: Tannins from oak bark bind to collagen, slow process taking months, produces supple and durable leather, traditional method

name: Chrome tanning: chromium salt curing
note: Chromium sulfate rapidly tans hides, produces softer leather than vegetable tanning, faster but requires chemical control

name: Alum tanning: mineral salt curing
note: Alum and salt pickle hides, faster than vegetable tanning, less durable, primarily for light leather goods

name: Currying: leather finish dressing
note: Oil dressing and working of leather after tanning, imparts finish and handling, essential finishing step

name: Splitting: leather layering
note: Separating hide into grain and buff layers, enables utilisation of full hide, requires sharp hand knives or mechanical blade

name: Embossing: surface pattern pressing
note: Hot press with pattern die creates surface texture, replicates grain or adds decoration, mechanical equipment by 1890s

name: Lasting machine: shoe fitting
note: Pneumatic or mechanical clamps pull upper leather over wooden last, tension nails sole attachment, eliminates hand work

name: Mechanised shoemaking: factory production
note: Chain of specialized machines and workers, division of labour, higher speed and lower cost, emerged in America mid-1800s

name: Rubber soles: vulcanised footwear
note: Vulcanised rubber soles reduce cost and improve water resistance, attached by cements or nailing, increasingly common from 1890s

name: Safety match: controlled ignition
note: Phosphorus on match strip, ignition requires friction on box strip, much safer than friction matches, Swedish invention 1844

name: Friction match: white phosphorus tip
note: White phosphorus mixed with oxidiser at stick tip, ignites spontaneously in air, dangerous but widespread in 19th century

name: Safety razor: guarded blade shaving
note: Thin steel blade held in guard, Gillette patent 1901, replaceable blade and guard system, transformed male grooming

name: Razor blade: replaceable steel cutting
note: Stamped and honed thin steel blade, consumable product, razor-blade business model generates recurring revenue

name: Toothbrush: hair bristle cleaning
note: Natural bristles set in wooden handle, Chinese technology known early, mass production in Europe from late 1800s

name: Mass-produced soap: standardised bars
note: Standardised formulation and cutting, wrapped and branded, Procter and Gamble transforms soap into mass-market good

name: Shampoo: hair cleansing liquid
note: Liquid soap formulation specifically for hair, emerges in early 20th century, mass production and branding key factors

name: Comb: hair grooming tool
note: Horn or bone cut into teeth, traditional technology, mass production emerges in 1800s with celluloid versions

name: Mirror: reflective glass surface
note: Mercury backing silvered glass, produced in quantity by medieval period, tin-amalgam backing emerges as alternative

name: Button: horn material
note: Shaped horn disc, drilled and edges finished, traditional high-quality material, medieval production

name: Button: bone material
note: Carved bone disc, fine quality and good durability, medieval production standard

name: Button: shell material
note: Mother-of-pearl and other shells cut into discs, lustrous appearance, waterborne trade commodity

name: Button: celluloid plastic material
note: Molded celluloid sheets stamped into buttons, cheaper and easier than natural materials, emerges in 1870s

name: Pin: sewing fastener
note: Drawn wire with point and head, hand-made labour-intensive process, medieval production by thousands

name: Needle: sewing implement
note: Polished iron or steel with eye, essential tool before sewing machines, hand-forged labour-intensive

name: Spectacle frame: eye support structure
note: Horn or metal frame holding optical lenses, nose bridge and arms, emerged in medieval period with mass production in 1800s

name: Watch case: portable timepiece housing
note: Protective case for pocket watch, brass with decorative engraving or gold cases, industrial production emerges in 1800s

name: Fountain pen: reservoir writing
note: Internal ink reservoir and feed system, iridium or gold nib, Waterman patent 1884 creates commercial success, transforms business writing

name: Ballpoint pen: ball-point writing
note: Small steel ball in socket, ink flows as ball rotates, Hungarian invention 1938, mass production challenges overcome by 1950s

name: Pencil: graphite and clay mixture
note: Ground graphite and clay mixed and fired, Conté and others develop proportions and hardness grades

name: Eraser: rubber pencil mark removal
note: Rubber abrasion removes graphite, cap-mounted or pencil-top versions, mass production emerges in late 1800s

name: Paperclip: bent wire fastener
note: Wire bent into overlapping loops, simple but effective, mass production by 1900s enables cheap office supplies

name: Stapler: metal wire fastener machine
note: Lever mechanism bends staple through papers, powered by hand, emerges in late 1800s as office automation

name: Drawing pin: short fastening point
note: Short point with wide head, brass or steel, holds paper to boards without permanent damage

name: Envelope: paper folded container
note: Paper folded and gummed, gummed flap seals contents, mass production by 1850s transforms postal efficiency

name: Gummed envelope flap: adhesive sealing
note: Starch-based adhesive applied to flap, dries to enable moistening, improvement over wax seals and tape

name: Postcard: prepaid correspondence
note: Thin card with pre-printed postage, emerges as cheap alternative to letters, mass-produced by 1870s

name: Printed playing card: mass-produced game
note: Hand-painted precedes printing, printing press enables mass production, stiff card and artistic design

name: Board game: printed game on board
note: Printed game board with rules and pieces, mass production of family entertainment, 19th century emergence

name: Jigsaw puzzle: dissectable picture
note: Printed image on wood or cardboard, hand-sawed or die-cut into interlocking pieces, emerges in 18th century as education and entertainment

name: Doll: articulated child plaything
note: Articulated limbs and face, wood or cloth construction, mass production with porcelain heads emerges in 19th century

name: Tin toy: stamped metal plaything
note: Stamped and lithographed tin plate toy, jointed or wheeled, German and Japanese production emerges in late 1800s

name: Clockwork toy: spring-driven mechanism
note: Spring-wound mechanism drives gears and linkages, walking or mechanical action, premium toy for wealthy children

name: Bicycle: mass-produced consumer good
note: Chain drive and pneumatic tyres, mass production enables affordability, transforms personal transport from 1890s

name: Camera: mass-produced photographic device
note: Fixed-focus simple lens, roll film, Kodak Brownie 1900 makes photography accessible to masses

name: Gramophone: sound recording reproduction
note: Needle-vibration pickup playing wax cylinder or disc, horn amplification, emerges in 1890s and becomes major consumer product

name: Radio set: wireless receiver entertainment
note: Crystal set or valve receiver and loudspeaker, mass production transforms home entertainment, major emergence in 1920s

name: Vacuum flask: thermal insulation
note: Double-walled glass with vacuum between, reflective surfaces, Thermos trade name, emerges in 1900s for portable hot beverages

name: Tin can: sealed metal container
note: Rolled and soldered tin plate, preserves food and other goods, mass production from 1810s onwards

name: Paper bag: folded container
note: Kraft paper folded and glued, bottom gussets for capacity, replaces cloth sacks for retail goods

name: Cardboard box: folded laminate container
note: Laminated paper sheets glued and folded, replaces wooden crates for many applications, mass production by 1870s

name: Corrugated box: fluted paper structure
note: Wavy paper core between flat faces, light and strong, enables efficient shipping, emerges in 1890s

name: Bottle: glass container
note: Hand-blown or later molded glass, seals and preserves liquids, mass production by 1870s

name: Crown cork: crimped bottle seal
note: Crimped tin cap with cork liner, seals carbonated beverages, bottling machine applies caps, invented 1891

name: Screw cap: threaded closure
note: Threaded metal cap screws onto grooved bottle neck, reusable and reversible, evolves from wood to plastic

name: Tube for toothpaste: extrudable container
note: Collapsible metal tube with sealed cap, contents extruded by squeezing, enables portable toothpaste

name: Capability: reliable electric motor
note: Prerequisite placeholder for electric motor power availability in textile machinery
